originality.rationale: The full published motivating paper studies maximal nine-site convex-hull volume, not the covering radius after site deletion. Full readable prior related results about the intact nine-site body concern intact Euclidean inball radii and extremal ellipsoids; their formulas do not entail the new quadrilateral facets after erasure, the orbit-resolved pair of spherical covering radii, or the unique robust minimax at r=2/3. Search returned these as the closest semantic matches. Classical covering tables address ordinary n-site covering without adversarial deletion from an initial nine-site family. Equivalent historical fault-tolerant results may be unindexed.

value.rationale: A one-site failure is a natural robust spherical-covering optimization, with two inequivalent site orbits. The complete sharp r-dependent one-erasure coverage and the unique symmetric-family optimum at r=2/3 differ from established global nine-vertex volume and intact-body inradius/ellipsoid optima. This identifies a structural phase boundary and a motivated exact invariant for a well-studied geometric family rather than an arbitrary isolated computation.
